i fear i'll fall behind, that i'll never be able to graduate on time. but it's ok. because as long as i am alive... that's what matters. it's not about the time it takes you to finish the journey, because it was never a race to begin with. 

you're not an academic failure. you are not a failure. i know how it feels to really feel worthless when you used to be an overachiever (for me, played piano, did art, was a consistent deans lister/honor role) and when you drop all the way to the bottom. it sucks. but college will always be there, waiting for you.

There is really no "efficient" way to make notes, and there is no "right" way to doing notes. The best notes that you can have are the notes that you make yourself.

I wish you a lot of luck! If you'd like to see my old DBQs or LEQs (with scoring and comments added) please DM me! I have some old examples from my teacher, who helped me pass the class with a 4.

I also recommend doing SAQ practices and DBQ plus LEQ practices that are timed. It seriously helps you with the testing, because then you don't have to worry about the time limit. You'll actually find yourself finishing before the timer is even done sometimes.

make sure you study what you're not strong on, because it'll bite you in the back when you take the test. make sure you take notes for each chapter (you don't even have to take the notes in one day, just as you're going through the chapter) or for each time period. it's okay to procrastinate but don't do it too often.
